diagnostic_evidence.quote:
An operator $T:C(\Omega)\to C(\Omega)$ is called a \emph{positive $\varepsilon$-contraction} if for any $g\in C(\Omega)$,
\[
    \|g^{+}-Tg\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)}
    \le (1-\varepsilon)\|g^{+}\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)}.
\]

issues.failure_explanation: The definition of positive $\varepsilon$-contraction only gives an $L^\infty$ norm bound on $g^{+}-Tg$. It does not imply the pointwise inequality $0\le g^{+}(x)-Tg(x)$ used in the proof. Without this pointwise bound (condition (C1)), the symmetrized operator $Sg=Tg-T(-g)$ need not be a balanced $\varepsilon$-contraction. A counterexample exists on a two-point domain. The actual operator $T_\varepsilon$ satisfies (C1), so the conclusion holds for it, but the lemma as stated is false.

failure_location.quote:
Applying the positive $\varepsilon$-contraction property to $g$ and $-g$ gives, for all $\bm{x}\in\Omega$,
\[
    0\le g^{+}(\bm{x})-Tg(\bm{x})
    \le (1-\varepsilon)\|g^{+}\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)}\le (1-\varepsilon)\|g\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)},
\]

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis that $T$ satisfies condition (C1) ($0\le Tg\le g^{+}$) to the lemma, or define positive $\varepsilon$-contraction to include this pointwise bound.
issues.overall_effect: The lemma is false as stated, but its application to $T_\varepsilon$ remains valid because $T_\varepsilon$ satisfies the missing pointwise condition. No main result is lost, but the formal statement is incorrect.
issues.title: Symmetrization lemma assumes pointwise bound not in definition
issues.why_classification: The missing hypothesis is already established for the operator $T_\varepsilon$ used in the paper, so a local edit to the lemma suffices to preserve all main results.

issues.failure_explanation: For $d>1$, $\Psi$ is an average of one-dimensional trapezoids. It is zero only if all coordinates have $\psi=0$, i.e., all coordinates lie outside $[-r,r]$. Thus $\Gamma_Q(x)$ can be positive even when $x$ is outside $rQ$ (e.g., one coordinate far outside, another near the center). This violates the required support property $\Gamma_Q(x)=0$ for $x\notin rQ$. Consequently, the proof's claim that $\Gamma=0$ outside $\cup rQ_i$ is false, and the overlap bound $\sum \Gamma \le 2^d$ fails. $T_\varepsilon$ may be positive at points where $g(x)$ is small or negative, so condition (C1) fails. This invalidates Lemma T positive and the construction.

failure_location.quote:
If instead
\[
\bmx\notin \bigcup_{i=1}^{n_{g,\varepsilon}} rQ_{g,\varepsilon,i},
\]
then $\Gamma_{Q_{g,\varepsilon,i}}(\bmx)=0$ for all $i$, and hence
\begin{equation}
T_\varepsilon g(\bmx)=0 .
\end{equation}

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the average $\Psi$ with a cutoff that is a product of one-dimensional trapezoids (or otherwise has support exactly $rQ$), and adjust the network realization and width/depth analysis accordingly. This changes the construction and likely the width bounds.
issues.overall_effect: The main theorem for $d>1$ is unproven; the fixed-width construction fails. The central result is invalid for general $d$.
issues.title: Cutoff function via average does not vanish outside rQ
issues.why_classification: The defect invalidates the core construction for $d>1$. Repair requires a new cutoff function with correct support, likely increasing width or depth, so the advertised fixed-width scheme and main theorem are not preserved without major changes.
